description: Exact overlapping string search with Galil–Giancarlo's heavy remembered-prefix refinement of Colussi.

source.title: On the Exact Complexity of String Matching: Upper Bounds
source.source_license: Copyright belongs to the cited authors and publisher. Mathematical algorithm descriptions only; independent implementation and workload.

workspace.meaning: Fixed text staging where used, pattern storage, Colussi/Galil-Giancarlo tables, and bounded local state.

contract.preprocessing: Construct the Colussi h, next, and shift tables for the pattern with an out-of-alphabet sentinel at position m.
contract.initial_run: ell is the last index in the initial run of pattern[0]; if the whole pattern is constant, use a streaming run-count search.
contract.heavy_resumption: After a remembered-prefix overlap and i=0, scan from last+1 for pattern[0]. If the run is too short or the following symbol is not pattern[ell+1], advance past the scanned run; otherwise resume with i=1 and remember the prefix through ell+1.
contract.text_end: The remembered-prefix scan stops at text_length and treats end-of-text as a mismatch without reading outside the input.
contract.result_bounds: At most 4096 matches; sum of offsets is below 2^23, so the packed result is below 2^49 and fits signed 64-bit.
contract.complexity: O(m) preprocessing time and space, O(n) search time; at most 4n/3 text comparisons for the nonconstant branch as stated by the source.
contract.error_precedence: Validate the input pointer, parseable length, header, exact packed length, and symbol ranges before searching.
